title: Mechanical Testing of Mouse Carotid Arteries: from Newborn to Adult
protocol: Turn on the air tank and myograph control boxes.
Start the MyoView software (Danish Myotechnology).
Load the appropriate diameter calibration file in the software.
Load the inflation protocol file for the first protocol.
Name the data file for saving.
Choose the required cannulae and suture size depending on mouse age.
Mount the cannulae in the test system carefully without applying excessive force (> 1 N) to the force transducer.
Fill the inflow bottle with 150 mL of physiological saline solution (PSS).
Fill the bath and inflow tubing with PSS.
Fill the outflow tubing halfway with PSS.
Place the filled bath on the inverted microscope stage when the temperature reaches 37.5 °C.
Zero the force transducer using MyoView software.
Sacrifice the mouse using approved euthanasia methods (CO2 asphyxiation).
Secure the mouse by taping the hands and feet to a dissecting board and place under a dissecting microscope.
Open the chest to expose the right and left carotid arteries using dissecting scissors and curved forceps.
Carefully clear fat and nearby tissue with curved forceps and fine tweezers until the full length of both carotids from the aorta to the common carotid bifurcation can be visualized.
Keep the arteries moist with PSS during the dissection procedure.
Cut a piece of 7-0 suture to the desired length using digital calipers and dissection scissors.
Lay the suture on the vessel.
Use an 18 G needle dipped in activated charcoal to mark the ends of the suture on the vessel.
Make sure that the complete length of the artery is lying in a single horizontal plane.
Take a picture of each carotid using a camera connected to the dissection microscope.
Measure the in vivo length using Image J software.
Use a syringe attached to an 18 G needle to inject PSS into the left ventricle and clear all blood out of the carotid arteries.
Cut the carotids at the charcoal markers using micro-scissors.
Place the cut carotids in a petri dish with a small amount of PSS.
Remove any fat from the outside of the arteries.
Let equilibrate for 2 - 3 minutes.
Take a picture of each artery and use Image J software to measure the ex vivo length.
Calculate the in vivo stretch ratio using the in vivo and ex vivo lengths.
Place the carotids in a microfuge tube filled with PSS until ready for testing.
Place the heated, filled bath under the dissection microscope.
Use the micrometer to bring the cannula tips together until they are just touching.
Record this value as the "zero length" of the micrometer.
Tie a small loop of suture with a loose overhand knot on each end of the cannulae.
Grasp one end of an artery using fine tweezers and place it in the bath.
Hold one end of the artery with two tweezers and slip it over one cannula.
For mice ≥ 21 days, tighten the suture knot after placing the vessel over the first cannula.
Repeat the process for the other side by grasping another end of the artery.
If mounting the second side is difficult, apply slight pressure to open up the artery.
For mice < 21 days, slide the vessel completely onto one side.
Bring the cannulae together until they are touching.
Slide the vessel back over the second cannula after separating the cannulae.
Tighten the suture knot on the second end.
Avoid twisting the artery during mounting.
Calculate the necessary micrometer reading for the artery to be at the measured ex vivo length.
Add 1.2 mm to the micrometer distance from the zero length to account for suture ties.
Measure the total unstretched artery length using digital calipers.
Set the micrometer to the calculated total unstretched artery length.
Check that the artery appears unstretched and the force is close to zero.
Calculate the necessary micrometer reading for the artery length between the suture ties at the measured in vivo stretch ratio.
Set the micrometer to this calculated length.
Begin testing protocols with the artery set at the "in vivo testing length".
Place the bath on the inverted microscope stage.
Position the central portion of the artery over the lens.
Focus on the edges of the artery wall.
Start diameter tracking in MyoView.
Check tracking of the outer diameter.
Ensure no fat is on the artery wall.
Adjust the contrast and brightness of the image.
Eliminate all bubbles from the fluid tubing.
Manually increase and decrease the pressure 3 times from zero to the maximum pressure for the specimen age in mouse arteries.
Set the pressure to 1/3 of the maximum pressure and stretch the artery axially 3 times by manually turning the micrometer from the in vivo stretch ratio to the maximum axial stretch.
Stretch the artery to a maximum axial stretch of 1.2 x the in vivo testing length for mice < 21 days.
Stretch the artery to a maximum axial stretch of 1.4 x the in vivo testing length for mice ≥ 21 days.

Run the appropriate inflation protocol for the specimen age to automatically increase pressure from zero to the maximum pressure 3 times while the vessel is at the in vivo stretch ratio, recording the data.
Stretch the artery to half of the maximum axial stretch and repeat the inflation protocol, recording the data in a new file.
Stretch the artery to the maximum axial stretch and repeat the inflation protocol, noting that the axial force should increase as pressure increases.
Set the pressure to 1/3 of the maximum pressure and manually stretch the artery to the maximum axial stretch 3 times at approximately 10 μm/sec, recording the data in a new file.
Increase the pressure to 2/3 of the maximum pressure and repeat the manual stretching protocol.
Set the pressure equal to the maximum pressure and perform the manual stretching protocol again.
Under the dissection microscope, hold one end of the artery with fine tweezers.
Cut 3 - 5 rings about 0.5 mm thick using a disposable scalpel.
Gently open up each ring into a circle using the tweezers.
Take pictures of the most circular rings for unloaded dimension measurements.
Use micro-scissors or a scalpel to cut each ring at one location and allow it to open into an arc.
Allow rings to equilibrate to their final shape for 10 minutes.
Take a picture of the open rings for opening angle measurements.
If desired, fix the remainder of the carotid artery in 10% formalin for histology processing.
Clean up the myograph system according to the manufacturer's instructions.
If there is a suspected clog in a cannula, clear it by inserting fine wire into the cannula tip.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl to reconstitute human recombinant leptin.
